summary:
EarthScope AI — Detecting Earth's Changing Trends with NASA Data

EarthScope AI is an interactive, AI-assisted Earth science analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps users investigate what is changing, where it is changing, how much it is changing, and whether observed trends are statistically significant.

Using NASA MERRA-2 datasets accessed through Giovanni, EarthScope AI analyzes historical temperature and precipitation observations from 2005–2025. Its Python statistical engine calculates annual measurements, linear trends, confidence intervals, and significance tests, while interactive visualizations compare environmental changes across Chennai and Hyderabad, India.

An integrated Gemini-powered scientific analyst translates calculated findings into accessible explanations while distinguishing estimated trends from statistically supported conclusions.

EarthScope AI aims to make NASA Earth science data more understandable and useful for students, researchers, educators, and environmentally curious communities.
details:
EarthScope AI — An AI-Assisted Earth System Trend Detective

The Problem

Earth's environmental systems are constantly changing. However, identifying meaningful trends requires access to reliable historical observations, appropriate statistical methods, and tools for comparing geographical regions.

Earth science datasets can be complex for non-specialists to explore. A rising or falling trend in a graph does not automatically establish a statistically significant change.

Our Solution

EarthScope AI is a publicly accessible web application that combines NASA Earth science data, reproducible statistical analysis, interactive visualization, and AI-assisted interpretation.

It addresses four questions:

  1. What is changing? Users can investigate temperature and precipitation.
  2. Where is it changing? The application compares Chennai and Hyderabad in India.
  3. How much is it changing? The statistical engine estimates trend magnitudes per decade.
  4. Is the change statistically significant? The application reports statistical tests and associated p-values.

NASA Data Used

The application uses NASA's Modern-Era Retrospective Analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2), accessed through NASA Giovanni.

Datasets:

  • M2TMNXSLV — Monthly 2-meter air temperature (T2M).
  • M2TMNXFLX — Monthly corrected total precipitation (PRECTOTCORR).

Analysis period: January 2005 through December 2025.

The application converts temperature from Kelvin to Celsius and monthly precipitation rates into accumulated precipitation totals before calculating annual statistics.

Technical Implementation

Backend and analysis: Python, Pandas, NumPy, and SciPy.

Visualization and interface: Gradio and Plotly.

AI interpretation: Google Gemini.

Deployment: Render, with source code maintained on GitHub.

NASA data is processed through the Python analysis pipeline. The resulting statistics are supplied to Gemini for natural-language interpretation. Gemini does not replace the statistical engine.

Demonstrated Capabilities

  • Visualization of 21 years of annual environmental observations.
  • Temperature and precipitation variable selection.
  • Chennai–Hyderabad regional comparisons.
  • Linear trend estimation and statistical significance reporting.
  • AI-assisted explanation of numerical results.
  • Public access through a web application.

Scientific Limitations

The present prototype uses two locations and two environmental variables. MERRA-2 represents environmental conditions on a relatively coarse geographical grid rather than measurements at every point within a city.

The significance tests are exploratory. Temporal autocorrelation, the selected analysis period, and spatial resolution may influence the estimated uncertainty. A nonsignificant result does not prove the absence of environmental change.

Potential Impact

EarthScope AI provides an approachable starting point for examining NASA environmental data. It can support education, exploratory scientific analysis, and communication of environmental trends.

Future versions could support user-defined regions, additional NASA variables, seasonal trend tests, spatial trend maps, and more advanced uncertainty analysis.
